unfinished: SECURITY IS ONE RECORD SHORT and is the only thing standing between the catalog and launch-gate row 1. High-traffic density: kitchen 12, av 13, computing 10, climate 10, security 9. Target is 10-15 each. Empty security subcategories: door lock, intercom, indoor camera, alarm panel, motion sensor, glass break sensor, gate opener. Best seeds, in order: (a) Aqara FP2 presence sensor — Wi-Fi, a nameable Aqara cloud, plus local HomeKit/Matter, so a clean D2 in the empty motion-sensor subcategory; (b) another Zooz or Ecolink Z-Wave sensor, which would be a second D1 and verifies fast because Zooz operates no cloud at all; (c) a Tuya Zigbee motion sensor with a Zigbee2MQTT page, which would be a third D3 — but see the SKU warning below. One agent, one afternoon, and row 1 is closed.

THE ONLY REMAINING LAUNCH-GATE ROW after that is /downgrades having an observed entry, and it cannot be scheduled — it needs a vendor to remove function from a shipped device and us to catch it. That is what the `watch` job is for and it has never been run. The closest live candidates are in this list: Anova (below), Grizzl-E, Withings. Running `watch` against the 131 published records is the only thing that will ever populate that page with something we caught rather than recorded.

HOW TO HUNT D3, now that it is known. D3 went 1 -> 3 in one wave, and the method is the finding: brief the agent at the INDEX, not the device. zigbee2mqtt.io and devices.esphome.io publish per-model pages keyed to exact model numbers, maintained continuously, with git history you can cite as maintenance evidence — which is exactly the 'cited, maintained guide for that exact model' the bar demands. Also OpenWrt's hardware table (keyed to model AND revision) and LocalTuya/Tuya Local. Seven waves never found a D3 because none was told where the guides live.

AND THE TRAP IN HUNTING D3, which cost wave 8 two candidates. An active hobbyist liberation project does NOT imply the device is cloud-dependent as sold — it usually means the device is pleasant to integrate. Both the MOES BHT-002-GBLW thermostat and the Winix C545 purifier were seeded as D3 on the strength of thriving ESPHome projects, and both manufacturers' own manuals document full local operation from the physical controls. They are D2. Confirm cloud dependency from the manual before believing it.

WHITE-LABEL ZIGBEE HAS AN IDENTITY PROBLEM the catalog will keep meeting, because it is the vein D3 runs through. tuya-ts0215a-sos-button is keyed to its Zigbee fingerprint, not a brand, because the same hardware sells as Clouree, RSH-SOS05, Woox R7054 and Nedis depending on importer and month. Easy to source at fingerprint level (the Zigbee2MQTT page), nearly impossible at SKU level. Key these records to the fingerprint, name the rebrands in notes, and carry a retail listing as an example rather than as the identity.

TAXONOMY DECISION OWED (a human call, per PRINCIPLES §6): security has no subcategory for a single-button wireless SOS/panic button. tuya-ts0215a-sos-button is filed under `key fob` as the closest fit, which is a stretch — both are small battery-powered wireless security remotes, but one summons help and the other unlocks a door. A `panic button` subcategory would describe the family accurately. Do not add it unilaterally; taxonomy changes are a human decision.

ANOVA is a live ledger candidate, reported but UNSOURCED — do not score it until it is. The kitchen agent found: an August 2024 subscription for app remote control (announced 2024-08-14, effective 2024-08-21, new accounts only, existing users grandfathered free), and simultaneously a plan to end app and cloud support entirely for first-generation Precision Cookers effective September 2025, which was REVERSED on 2025-01-16 after backlash with a commitment to indefinite support. That shape — a real threat to already-sold hardware that did not materialise — is scale 1, the same rung Withings sits on. It needs its own sources before it goes in; the orchestrator did not verify them this run. anova-precision-cooker-3 is published at D2 with vendor_risk 0.

BAMBU LAB is still the strongest unscored ledger candidate and has now been carried through three waves. The January 2025 mandatory-authorisation firmware dispute is dated and covered by Hackaday, Tom's Hardware, All3DP and 3D Printing Industry. bambu-lab-a1 sits at vendor_risk 0. Probably a 1 (disputed/narrow) since Developer Mode still gives local control — but decide it on sources, and note the tier is NOT affected either way. Sonos took about twenty minutes to source and score this run; Bambu is no harder.

QNAP owed a ledger DECISION, not research, and has now been carried through four waves because nobody will make it. The question: does a forced security patch count as removing function from shipped devices? A defensible answer, offered as a recommendation rather than applied: motive is not the test, but loss of function is — so a forced patch that removes NO function is not a ledger incident and belongs in `firmware_ota_forced` (which already exists and already says the vendor can reach into the device), while a forced patch that DOES remove function scores on the normal scale, annotated with the security motive so a reader can tell 'this vendor monetises your device' from 'this vendor will reach in without asking'. That split uses machinery the schema already has. It needs a human to adopt or reject it.

THE REVIEW PASS KEEPS EARNING ITS KEEP. Wave 8 re-derived three deciding facts and two produced changes (the APC citation defect, the unresolvable GE dormant-radio question); wave 7 checked three and all three did. Ten of thirteen wave-8 records were not re-derived. Target negative claims and citations that look too specific — those are where both waves' defects were.

GE FAMILY RECORDS: the dormant-radio question is unresolved and now scopes both records rather than undermining them. What would settle it: the Connect+ module's own FCC grant (not found on fccid.io) or a teardown photo of an Optional WiFi control board. If the module holds the grant, the radio is in the module and both records can be widened to cover the Optional WiFi line. BACKLOG also still wants equivalent family records for Whirlpool, LG and Samsung, whose connected-feature naming differs (SmartThings, ThinQ).

THE DUMB DISHWASHER IS DISAPPEARING, and the site should say so somewhere a reader will see it. Wave 8 went looking for a current Bosch dishwasher without Home Connect and there is not one: every current 100/300/500/800-series SKU ships it as standard, and the models without it (Ascenta SHX3AR75UC, 100-series SHXM4AY55N) are marked no-longer-available on Bosch's own site. That is a finding about the market, not a failed seed, and it is exactly the kind of thing /updates or a domain intro exists to carry.

ONE REJECTION STILL POINTS NOWHERE: dji-neo needs a drone alternative. gopro-hero13-black serves the two action-camera rejections but is not a drone. A sub-$500 drone that flies and records without app activation is the target; if none exists, the honest finding is that the subcategory has no passing device and the record should say so rather than stay blank.

Cressi Leonardo (dive computer, D0) abandoned in wave 6 after ~10 failed fetches — cressi.com serves a broken TLS cert and retailer mirrors all blocked. Still the natural D0 contrast to shearwater-peregrine at D2. Untouched in waves 7 and 8.

Two records blocked on purchasability, not tier evidence, and untouched for three waves: a GRI 100/110 wired door contact (passive two-wire reed switch, trade distributors only — would also help the security count) and a non-smart LED bulb (the record 'dumb light bulb' searchers want; Feit/GE/Sylvania/Signify all serve JS-rendered pages).

woods-50015 has a dead Class A source (southwire.com catalogue PDF) with no Wayback snapshot. Per archive-sources.mjs's own words, a source with no snapshot and no live page cannot support a claim: re-source it or withdraw what it supports.

/updates/ is the page most likely to trip the weight rule next. 48 KB against 35 KB free + 1 KB per record listed, and it grows with the changelog rather than the catalog — corrections on existing devices add bytes without adding rows. It needs a cutoff or pagination before that crosses.

SEARCH BUDGET is no longer the constraint for verification: wave 8's three agents used about 95 searches between them against the 200 cap. Seeded lists did that. Genuine discovery — hunting a tier or a domain with no candidate list — is still where the cap would bind.
